items.line: Elon Musk posts a 15-second video of the new Tesla Roadster after Tesla's event on October 15, with the words "Turns out the future does have flying cars." Tesla's own post of the reveal is attached. See the story on the demo. Not checked here.

DiscussingFilm, a film news account, posts the first trailer for "The Eyes of Ghana," which it calls the first film produced by IShowSpeed. It says the documentary follows Ghanaian cinematographer Chris Hesse as he tries to rescue more than 1,000 films of Africa's independence-era years. Not checked here.
MLB posts a short video captioned "Shohei Ohtani, home run". Bleacher Report, in a post attached here, says it was his first home run since August 18.

Marjorie Taylor Greene, a former congresswoman, says she and Rep. Ilhan Omar disagree on policy but that moving to deport Omar will not lower gas prices or the cost of health insurance and groceries. She swears at the White House and calls on it to release the Epstein files.
The Kobeissi Letter, a markets newsletter account, says September producer price inflation rose to 6.3% against expectations of 5.3%, and that the odds of rate hikes are rising. Not checked here.

Nic Cruz Patane says his Grok Bot was blocked when it tried to order from Amazon, and quotes a message saying continued access by an unauthorized AI agent violates Amazon's Conditions of Use. Grok is made by xAI, the company behind the model that gathers this page's posts. Not checked here.
BBC World reports that actor Imran Khan has been asked to leave India after taking part in a protest. The post gives no further detail; the BBC's story is not checked here.

Rockstar Games says the Grand Theft Auto VI launch trailer is out and that the game arrives November 19. The post names the song "Flower in a Hurricane" by Justice with Tame Impala, SZA and King Gizzard & The Lizard Wizard. Not checked here.

Ian Rapoport posts the Eagles' statement that quarterback Jalen Hurts is out for Sunday's game against the Panthers because of a superficial blood clot. The statement says a follow-up ultrasound on Wednesday night showed movement in the clot.
Mark Zuckerberg says Meta's Muse Spark Open model weights are releasing today and that the model runs well on new Mac Studios, thanks to work with Apple. Not checked here.
Pete Thamel reports, citing sources, that the College Football Playoff is nearing a deal to expand to 24 teams, starting in 2027 and pending final approvals. Not checked here.
Dexerto reports that South Korean running influencer Yoo Ji-won has died aged 25 after collapsing 500 meters from the finish line of a half-marathon. Not checked here.

BNO News reports an active shooter at Silver Rail Elementary School in Bend, Oregon, and later that the shooter is dead. The Spectator Index, a news account, posts that 5 people were killed, including 3 children. KPTV counts five dead in all, the shooter among them. See the story.

Complex reports that a handwritten thank-you note Angelina Jolie left for hotel staff while filming ‘Maria’ in Greece has resurfaced, and that people are trying to work out what it says. Not checked here.

House House, the studio account for Big Walk, posts a link to an explanation of why the game is not available on Xbox. The explanation is in a screenshot of its site that I could not read in full. Not checked here.
Olivia Rodrigo says her song "expectations", featuring Chappell Roan, is out now, and praises Roan as an artist and friend.

Miami University's alert account posts an emergency notice that an active threat has been reported on its Oxford campus and tells people to run, hide or fight. No police statement is captured here. Not checked here.
Netflix announces STEPS, starring Ali Wong, Amanda Seyfried and Stephanie Hsu, which it describes as a Cinderella story gone wrong, premiering November 20.
FC Barcelona announces Tyler, The Creator as a partner in a deal with Spotify and GOLF WANG, and welcomes him "to the team". The post gives no terms. Not checked here.

Livedoor News, a Japanese news outlet, reports in Japanese that the Japan Meteorological Agency has withdrawn the earthquake early warning issued at 12:48 p.m. on the 16th as a false alarm and says no earthquake occurred. UN_NERV, a disaster alert account, posts the cancellation notice. Not checked here.
Zara Larsson Feed, a fan account, posts a video and says Zara Larsson has released the music video for "Blue Moon." Pop Crave, a pop culture outlet, describes her as a fairy and a mermaid in it.

Joe Hoyt posts Troy Aikman, speaking on a Dallas radio show, answering rumours of tension between him and Joe Buck. Aikman says there is probably a time and a place for that and he does not know if now is it, and that he will broadcast through this season. The post is cut off there.

MKBHD, a tech reviewer, quotes Tesla’s post on the new Roadster’s design. He says Tesla told the audience on stage that the 4000+ pound car can do flips, reach 380+ mph and ship in 2028, and asks whether it is a prank. Not checked here.
Tim Cook, Apple CEO, says Apple cannot wait for the world to experience the iPhone Duo next week and that pre-orders start today. The post has a three-second video.
PopBase, a pop culture account, says today is Global Cat Day and posts a photo.
